title: Linux_Remaiten_Botnet_Investigation_df2
description: Investigate and respond to the Linux/Remaiten botnet activity on the network.

levels.title: Introduction
levels.content: The network has experienced unusual traffic patterns and potential unauthorized access. Your task is to investigate and respond to this incident.

levels.title: Get Access
levels.cloud_content:
You have SSH access to the victim host with the following credentials:
- Host: victim (192.168.80.100)
- Username: ubuntu
- Password: ubuntu

Enter the word 'start' to begin the investigation.
levels.local_content:
You have SSH access to the victim host with the following credentials:
- Host: victim (192.168.80.100)
- Username: ubuntu
- Password: ubuntu

Enter the word 'start' to begin the investigation.

levels.title: Identify Suspicious Service
levels.content:
Identify and investigate an unauthorized or suspicious service responsible for periodic external communication.

**Question:** What is the name of the suspicious service that is periodically communicating with an external host?
levels.solution:
Check running services and their network connections. Look for services that connect to external hosts on non-standard ports.

Use the command `systemctl status bot-beacon.service` to verify the service status.

The suspicious service is named `bot-beacon.service`.

hints.title: First hint title
hints.content: Check running services and their network connections. Look for services that connect to external hosts on non-standard ports.

hints.title: Second hint title
hints.content: Use commands like `systemctl list-units --type=service` and `netstat -tulnp` to identify suspicious services.

hints.title: Third hint title
hints.content: Use the command `systemctl status bot-beacon.service` to verify the service status.

levels.title: Identify Abnormal Traffic Service
levels.content:
Identify the service responsible for generating abnormal volumes of network traffic.

**Question:** What is the name of the service generating abnormal volumes of network traffic?
levels.solution:
Examine network connections and look for services sending multiple connections to the same destination.

Use the command `systemctl status bot-flood.service` to verify the service status.

The service generating abnormal volumes of network traffic is named `bot-flood.service`.

hints.title: First hint title
hints.content: Examine network connections and look for services sending multiple connections to the same destination.

hints.title: Second hint title
hints.content: Use commands like `netstat -tulnp` and `ss -tulnp` to identify services with high network activity.

hints.title: Third hint title
hints.content: Use the command `systemctl status bot-flood.service` to verify the service status.

levels.title: Determine Persistence Mechanism
levels.content:
Determine how the suspicious service is automatically started after reboot.

**Question:** What is the name of the systemd service responsible for the persistence of the suspicious service?
levels.solution:
Investigate systemd timers and services that might be related to the suspicious service.

Use the command `systemctl status system-update-checker.timer` to verify the timer status.

The systemd service responsible for the persistence of the suspicious service is named `system-update-checker.timer`.

hints.title: First hint title
hints.content: Investigate systemd timers and services that might be related to the suspicious service.

hints.title: Second hint title
hints.content: Use commands like `systemctl list-timers` and `systemctl list-unit-files` to identify persistence mechanisms.

hints.title: Third hint title
hints.content: Use the command `systemctl status system-update-checker.timer` to verify the timer status.
